props.description: A slab door on the north wall, banded in tarnished iron. It has no handle on this side.

A stone sarcophagus on a low dais. The lid is carved with a robed figure whose face has been deliberately chiselled away. The seam is scored with fresh scratches, as though something has worked at it from beneath.
An iron brazier burning low and green. It gives heat but no smoke.
A second brazier, matching the first, its flame guttering as if in a draught you cannot feel.
A squat pillar, its base ringed with old wax.
A squat pillar. Something has scratched a tally into it — eleven marks, the last one incomplete.
A spill of fallen masonry where the ceiling has given way.

props.revealHint: A votive alcove behind a loose facing stone, level with the sarcophagus. Careful examination of the sarcophagus or the surrounding wall would find it.
props.description: A shallow alcove behind a displaced stone, holding a clay votive lamp and a bundle of grave-cloth gone black with age.
A small iron-bound reliquary, set near the stair they came down. The latch is not locked.
A warped barrel shoved against the west wall, its hoops rusted shut.
A splintered crate, empty except for straw gone to dust.
A plain coffin stood on end in the corner, the lid still nailed.
A clay pot, the kind grave-goods come in, its mouth sealed with wax.
A tall vase, chipped at the lip, holding nothing but grit.
An iron bucket beside the west brazier, dry.
A stone fox, sitting, watching the north door. One ear is broken off.
A horse statue, smaller than life, its rider long since knocked away.
A standing lantern, unlit, between the east brazier and the north wall.
A small shrine jammed into the north-east corner, its niche empty.
A wooden chair facing the north door, as if someone had been waiting.
A yellowed skull on the flagstones, missing the jaw.
A ribcage, animal or child, it is hard to say, slumped against the east wall.
A thick cobweb spanning the west wall, grey with dust.
A faded banner on the east wall, the device worn to a stain.
A huddle of candles on the north wall, burned down to nubs.
The stair the party came down, open to the grey light of the ruin above.

dmNotes.overview: A single burial chamber beneath a ruined chapel. Cold, close. The only exit the party knows of is the stair behind them to the south.
dmNotes.sensory: Air like a held breath. The braziers hiss. Every sound arrives a half-second late, as if the room is deciding whether to allow it.
dmNotes.theSarcophagus: A goblin scavenger named Vessk crawled in through a collapsed shaft two days ago, levered the lid aside looking for grave-goods, and got trapped when it settled back. It is hungry, frightened, and will come out fighting. The scratches on the seam are its work.
dmNotes.theDoor: The north door opens onto a stair up into a long gallery. It is heavy and it sticks, and the copper lamp-key turns its lock — but it opens. Anything the player was told earlier about it being sealed was true of a door that had not been unlocked yet; do not restate it as though it still cannot open.
dmNotes.theSarcophagusOpened: Vessk is out and on the grid. However he got out is whatever the narration said — do not contradict it, and do not put him back. The sarcophagus held nothing else: no body, no occupant, no second thing clawing at the lid, just grave-dust in the bottom of a stone box. If the player looks inside or listens at it, that is what they find. The scratching has stopped, because the thing making it is in the room with them.

fires.lit: Lit green by two braziers that should have burned out centuries ago.
fires.moved: The braziers have gone out — the green light is gone, and the cold in here is the cold of the stone.
